# Mātugāma Saṁyutta (SN 37)

**ID:** SN 37
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Mātugāma Saṁyutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Linked Discourses on Females
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn37
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mātugāma Saṁyutta* (SN 37) is the thirty-seventh collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, comprising thirty-four short discourses centering on women [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2003a]. The collection addresses topics such as the physical and moral factors that make a woman agreeable or disagreeable to a man (including beauty, wealth, ethical conduct, industriousness, and bearing children), as well as corresponding factors that attract women to men [Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003b; Cabezón 2017; Hazra 1994]. It details the kinds of suffering unique to women (*āveṇikāni dukkhāni*) that are not experienced by men, qualities like wide learning that benefit women, and the moral causes leading to rebirth in fortunate or unfortunate realms [SuttaCentral; Freedman 1977; Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003c]. The Venerable Anuruddha features prominently as an interlocutor in many of these suttas, inquiring about women's rebirths by means of his development of the divine eye (*dibbacakkhu*) [Bodhi 2003a; Bodhi 2003c]. Textual arrangements vary slightly among recensions: Burmese (*Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana*) and Siamese editions present suttas 5–24 as addressed to Anuruddha, whereas the Pali Text Society edition organizes the opening formulas differently [Bodhi 2003c].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify a full parallel to discourses SN 37.27–28 in the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (EĀ 35.4) [SuttaCentral]. In addition, computational analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse with the numerical collections of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, sharing the highest volume of text with the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), as well as the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), and *Aṭṭhakanipāta* (AN 8) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-linguistic alignments with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) and the Mahāyāna *Drumakinnararājaparipṛcchā-sūtra* [DharmaNexus].
